To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of rational numbers provides for a robust specification of 3-D geometric primitives; 2) rational arithmetic provides a closed system for the intersection of 3D spatial primitives; and 3) the rational specification of primitives provides a more robust implementation than the discretization methods that have been used in 2-D.

rational arithmetic is necessary and sufficient in order to implement robust three-dimensional spatial data structures and that the use of rational numbers is the best way to implement robust geometric primitives.

3D spatial database systems need robust geometric primitives; the robustness of geometric primitives can be achieved by using rational numbers to specify them; the robustness can be achieved in the implementation of spatial operations on these primitives by using rational arithmetic; the robustness is not achievable by extending the discretization methods of 2D spatial data types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of 3D spatial primitives that can be implemented robustly.
the development of 3D spatial database systems.
the implementation of 3D spatial primitives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of rational numbers is a necessary step in the design of 3D spatial primitives.
the use of rational numbers for defining geometric primitives provides a necessary and sufficient condition for the implementation of robust three-dimensional spatial data structures.
the use of rational numbers provides for robustness in the geometric primitives of three-dimensional spatial databases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of rational numbers provides a means of robust implementation for 3D primitives and operations.
the rational number theory provides the basis for the design of robust 3D primitives and operations.
we have provided a set of robust geometric primitives, a set of spatial data types and a set of spatial operations for 3D.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of rational numbers for defining 3D primitives is a robust approach.
the implementation of robust 3D geometric data types is possible and that it can be done using rational numbers.
rational number theory is applicable to 3D spatial database systems and that it provides for robustness.
